title: Optimize quantized kernels (INT8/FP8) + smoothquant/dequant fusion; scheduling + KV-cache continuous batching improvements
author: Asha Patel
description: Motivation: quantized inference (INT8/FP8) is a major cost / latency lever for our hosted and dedicated products. Previous flows paid too much overhead on dequant/quant switches and per-request scaling for smoothquant, and our scheduler+KV-cache interactions caused suboptimal batching for short-sequence workloads. This PR addresses three orthogonal areas with coordinated changes: 1) fused dequant+GEMM microkernel and FP8/INT8 code paths to remove redundant conversions, 2) eager smoothquant scaling fusion at model load time and better per-layer scale metadata, 3) scheduler heuristics + KV-cache hot-key awareness to improve continuous-batching packing for mixed-length traffic. Summary of changes: - Implemented fused dequant+matmul microkernel (x86/ampere GPU kernels) with INT8 input/FP16 accumulation fallback; when model uses FP8 weights we route through the new FP8-optimized kernel. - Introduced a smoothquant pre-scaler stage that applies per-channel scales during weight load and stores a compact scale vector; runtime path now skips runtime mul/div for most layers. - Added dequant-fusion passes to the compilation pipeline to collapse quant->dequant->matmul into a single op when the downstream kernel supports fusion. - Scheduler: added KV-cache awareness so requests that hit cache-heavy tokens are prioritized for lower-latency routing and grouped into separate continuous-batching pools to avoid polluting longer-sequence batches. - Continuous batching: enhanced packer to use sequence-length histogram and recent-latency signals; short sequences are packed more aggressively, long sequences are capped to ensure latency SLOs. - Tests/bench: added microbenchmarks for the fused kernels and end-to-end LLM throughput/latency harnesses. Checklist: - [x] Microkernel implementation and unit tests - [x] Compilation pass changes and integration tests - [x] Scheduler heuristics + e2e perf tests - [x] Docs (internal runtime notes) - [x] Benchmarks demonstrating improvements Performance results (internal benchmarks, resnet-llm-small & open-llm-7b-like traces): - INT8 fused kernel: 1.7-1.9x throughput increase vs baseline quant path; 10-18% p95 latency reduction under 96 token workload. - FP8 route: 1.4x throughput vs prior FP8 fallback path; memory transient allocations reduced ~28%. - End-to-end throughput uplift: 1.6x median across representative workloads; p95 latency improved 8-15% depending on traffic mix. Backwards compatibility & safety: - All changes gated behind feature flags and model-caps checks; if kernel fusion isn’t available we fallback to previous dequant+matmul path. - Added extensive fuzzing for quant edge cases and a regression suite against our evaluation prompts. Rollout plan: - Feature flag off in prod; gradual rollout to dedicated customers and internal canaries; monitor token-level quality/regression alerts and latency SLOs. Related: ENG-7123 (quant kernel roadmap), ENG-7189 (scheduler continuous batching), SUP-4382 (customer report about regressions in short-sequence latency).
